summary_of_change:
In operational reality, KeyCorp is executing a steady recovery following its post-2024 balance sheet restructuring enabled by Scotiabank’s ~$2.8B equity injection (14.9% stake, with regulatory filings submitted to move up to 19.99%). In Q2 2026, KeyCorp generated net income of $472.0M ($0.44 per diluted share, +26% YoY), driven by taxable-equivalent revenue of $1,960.0M (+6.8% YoY) and net interest income of $1,260.0M. Average loans expanded to $110.1B (+10.3% YoY in commercial C&I), while period-end client deposits reached $153.1B with a healthy 75% loan-to-deposit ratio.

Although Q2 sequential NIM expansion moderated to +2 bps (2.89%) due to short-term wholesale funding used to bridge rapid commercial loan growth during a seasonal deposit dip, underlying asset repricing remains intact. Non-interest fee income proved resilient at $700.0M, supported by record Wealth Management AUM of $74.2B (+15.5% YoY) and targeted middle-market bolt-on M&A (such as Clearwater Corporate Finance LLP). Net charge-offs were well-controlled at 42 bps, at the lower end of full-year 40–45 bps guidance.

Management re-affirmed and upgraded full-year 2026 guidance at the September 14, 2026 Barclays Conference: total revenue growth of ~8% YoY (over $7.5B baseline), NII growth of 9%–11%, average loan growth of 4%–5% (led by 8%–10% commercial growth), and an exit 4Q 2026 NIM of 3.00%–3.05%. With a GAAP CET1 ratio of 11.2%, KeyCorp repurchased $341M of shares in Q2 2026 under its $3.0B buyback authorization while maintaining its $0.205 quarterly dividend.
